newsitem.title: INDIA: India announces steps to bolster jute industry.
newsitem.headline: India announces steps to bolster jute industry.

text.p: India on Monday announced a set of measures to revive its ailing jute industry, a day after extending a law that forces many sectors to use jute packaging.

Vinod Malhotra, a senior Textiles Ministry official, told a news conference that the new strategy would focus on promoting non-traditional jute goods with export potential, regarded as vital to shore up the world's largest jute industry.
Malhotra said nearly 70 percent of the non-traditional, value-added products would be exported to meet a growing demand for environment-friendly products in Western markets.
"Export of jute in its present form is not really earning much foreign exchange, but with the value addition factor it would become a real money earner," he said.
In 1996/97 (July-June), India's jute exports more than doubled to 7.00 billion rupees ($190.56 million) from 3.23 billion rupees in 1992/93, Malhotra said.
India is the world's second largest jute exporter, controlling nearly 23 percent of the global market, he said.
"We plan to boost the production of diversified goods like shopping bags, wall hangings for interior decoration, textiles, floor coverings and decorative items," Malhotra said.
On Sunday, the government extended for another two years a 1987 law requiring the foodgrains, sugar and fertiliser industries to use jute in packaging.
Malhotra said value-added goods' share in total jute products would be raised to around 25 percent within the next three years, compared to its present level of about 15 percent.
The value of the Indian jute industry's total output is estimated at nearly 35 billion rupees.

Some 4.5 million people are employed in cultivating the crop and in other jute-related industries. India has 73 composite jute mills and 600 downstream factories, making it the world's largest jute manufacturer.
